A_trait: nectar reward / experimentally robbed versus unrobbed floral state
decision_note: Primary Digitalis experiment manually imposes nectar robbing, measures bumblebee behaviour and male/female reproductive output, and finds lower seed production in robbed plants. The manipulation is robbery state rather than an independently declared plant trait coordinate.
Authorea/preprint version of the Digitalis purpurea dataset published as SCHPRISMA-000564 / Ecology and Evolution DOI 10.1002/ece3.8068. Retain the version of record and exclude the duplicate report.

A_trait: flower size; pollen/stigma morphology; nectar production under aphid herbivory
decision_note: Primary Lonicera etrusca study shows aphid herbivory changes floral morphology, nectar, pollen/stigma function, pollination and fruit/seed reproduction. Herbivory is the upstream cause of floral change rather than a receiver response to one floral coordinate.

A_trait: flowering time; flower production; herbivory-induced flowering phenotype
decision_note: Primary Brassica nigra common-garden experiment manipulates herbivore identity and attack timing, measures flowering traits, pollinator visits, pollen-beetle colonization and seed fitness. It identifies context-dependent indirect interaction effects, not two matched response functions on a declared floral trait axis.
